articleTitle: Compact moving mechanism using ER fluid and piezoelectric element
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper proposes a compact moving mechanism using a piezoelectric element and ER fluid. This mechanism consists of a piezoelectric element, electrodes and ER fluid. This mechanism realizes minute displacement by controlling the timing of extension and contraction of the piezoelectric element and the timing of position retention by the position retention mechanism using the ER fluid. Since both the piezoelectric element and the ER fluid are driven by voltage, low-power operation can be expected. Results of some preliminary experiments are presented.

articleTitle: Deep Transfer Learning Feature Concatenation for Exam Cheating Detection Based on Footage Camera Recordings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Cheating during exams is an act that is violated in the academic integrity. Footage cameras can monitor online exam activities efficiently and thoroughly. Automatic detection of cheating during exams makes it easier for supervisors to monitor exam activities, but there is still potential for misdetection, especially if monitoring resources are limited. This paper optimizes the automatic detection of cheating during online exams by utilizing two surveillance cameras with different views. The deep transfer learning feature concatenation approach is used to obtain better feature representation. Compared to feature extraction methods using pre-trained models VGG16, VGG19, and Resnet50V. Cheating actions are recognized with LSTM and CNN classifiers. The proposed method shows that the combination of Resnet50 and CNN provides optimal accuracy for the best accuracy, recall, precision, and F1 score metrics.

articleTitle: Voice control interface for surgical robot assistants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Traditional control interfaces for robotic-assisted minimally invasive surgery impose a significant cognitive load on surgeons. To improve surgical efficiency, surgeon-robot collaboration capabilities, and reduce surgeon burden, we present a novel voice control interface for surgical robotic assistants. Our system integrates Whisper, state-of-the-art speech recognition, within the ROS framework to enable real-time interpretation and execution of voice commands for surgical manipulator control. The proposed system consists of a speech recognition module, an action mapping module, and a robot control module. Experimental results demonstrate the system’s high accuracy and inference speed, and demonstrates its feasibility for surgical applications in a tissue triangulation task. Future work will focus on further improving its robustness and clinical applicability.

articleTitle: Development of Cell Membrane Perforator for Large-Scale Application of Photochemical Cell Membrane Perforation by Continuous Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Photochemical cell membrane perforation is a technique that introduces substances directly into large numbers of cells and has a low cytotoxic effect. Among several cell modification techniques, this method is more efficient, since it can perforate a group of cells rather than an individual cell. It is also characterized by a high cell survival rate because the perforation is performed using oxidative treatment so that cells can repair themselves. To further expand this technology on a larger scale, we aimed to shift from batch processing to flow processing. In particular, the perforator, which had a flat shape in the past, was changed to a cylindrical shape, and a mechanism was developed for cell modification by passing a mixture of cells and transfection components between the perforator and two rotating cylinders on the receiving side.

articleTitle: Enhancing Disturbance-Rejection Performance of Wheeled Inverted Pendulum Systems with Knee-Wheel Integrated Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Mobile wheeled inverted pendulum (MWIP) vehicles are prone to lose maneuverability and attitude stability when encountering steep slopes or crossing ground obstacles due to their inherent unstable and underdriven dynamics. Therefore, the problem of anti-disturbance control has been a major issue in the control design of MWIP systems. In this study, we calculate the theoretical stabilization range of a first-order wheeled inverted pendulum to ensure the safe operation of the MWIP. Additionally, the knee joint degree of freedom is added on the basis of the first-order inverted pendulum to build a wheel-leg MWIP system. We introduced knee joint rotation when the robot is near the edge of losing control, which improves balance and enables obstacle crossing in complex environments. Simulations of balance control with a 4 cm and 5 cm radius semi-cylinder verified the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Locomotion Learning in a Musculoskeletal System through Reinforcement Learning of Joint Actions and LSTM Learning of Muscle Actions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: The study presents an innovative method for musculoskeletal modeling that leverages reinforcement learning (RL) alongside a simplified muscle model, enabling dynamic movements like running without needing pre-recorded data or preset calculations. The key goals are to create methods for generating running actions using a half-cheetah model and to adjust for variations in muscle redundancy and stiffness. By decoupling the learning of movement patterns from the efficient use of muscles, the approach simplifies the process, making it more understandable, easier to implement, and adjustable, while also reducing computational demands. The suggested model combines an RL agent, which observes the environment and determines the necessary torque for each joint. This torque is then transformed into muscle activations via a long shortterm memory neural network (LSTM) model. Preliminary findings indicate that this combined model replicates movement patterns similar to the half-cheetah model presented by the simulation framework MujoCo and achieves a running speed of $2.4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, slightly lower than the $2.9 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ achieved with joint motors. Although it consumes more energy, as shown by a Cost of Transport (CoT) of $\mathbf{3 . 4}$ compared to $\mathbf{1 . 5}$ for the joint motors model, the method proves to be suitable for integrating muscle functions. Future work will focus on developing a comprehensive 3D cheetah model to simulate various gaits and evaluate the scalability of this method. This will facilitate a detailed comparison between motor-driven and muscle-driven models in robotics. The main challenges to be addressed include ensuring data accuracy, optimizing parameters, and enhancing energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Embedded Image-to-Image Translation for Efficient Sim-to-Real Transfer in Learning-based Robot-Assisted Soft Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Recent advances in robotic learning in simulation have shown impressive results in accelerating learning complex manipulation skills. However, the sim-to-real gap, caused by discrepancies between simulation and reality, poses significant challenges for the effective deployment of autonomous surgical systems. We propose a novel approach utilizing image translation models to mitigate domain mismatches and facilitate efficient robot skill learning in a simulated environment. Our method involves the use of contrastive unpaired Image-toimage translation, allowing for the acquisition of embedded representations from these transformed images. Subsequently, these embeddings are used to improve the efficiency of training surgical manipulation models. We conducted experiments to evaluate the performance of our approach, demonstrating that it significantly enhances task success rates and reduces the steps required for task completion compared to traditional methods. The results indicate that our proposed system effectively bridges the sim-to-real gap, providing a robust framework for advancing the autonomy of surgical robots in minimally invasive procedures.
